question: Which man who did not die am I?
reference: Genesis 5:21-24; Hebrews 11:5; Jude 14-15 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Enoch No. 1')

clues: I was the seventh from Adam in the faithful line of Seth.
I walked with the true God for 300 years while raising a family.
Jude records that I prophesied about God coming with his myriads of holy ones.
Then I was no more, because God took me.

question: Which firstborn son am I?
reference: Genesis 4 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Cain')

clues: I worked the ground and brought some of its produce as an offering.
My brother's offering was looked on with favor and mine was not, and I burned with anger.
I lured my brother into the field and became the first man to shed human blood.
Marked and driven off to wander, I later built the first city and named it after my son.

question: Which nephew am I?
reference: Genesis 13; 19 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Lot')

clues: I left Ur and then Haran traveling with my uncle.
When our herdsmen quarreled, I chose the well-watered plain and pitched my tent near a wicked city.
Two angels had to grab me by the hand to pull me out before fire rained down.
My wife looked back and became a pillar of salt.

question: Which elder twin am I?
reference: Genesis 25-33 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Esau')

clues: I was born red and hairy, and I grew up to be a skilled hunter.
I sold my birthright to my younger brother for a bowl of red stew.
My father intended to bless me, but my brother took the blessing by disguising himself.
Years later I ran to meet that brother and wept on his neck instead of taking revenge.

question: Which son of Jacob am I?
reference: Genesis 37; 44; 49 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Judah No. 1')

clues: I talked my brothers into selling our younger brother to traders instead of killing him.
Later I offered to become a slave in Egypt in place of Benjamin.
My father's deathbed words said the scepter would not depart from me.
Both King David and the Messiah came from my tribe.

question: Which firstborn of Jacob am I?
reference: Genesis 37; 35:22; 49:3-4 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Reuben')

clues: I was the oldest of the twelve brothers.
I urged the others not to kill our brother but to throw him into a pit, planning to rescue him.
I lost my rights as firstborn because I lay with my father's concubine.
My father's blessing called me as unstable as water.

question: Which beloved wife am I?
reference: Genesis 29-35 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Rachel')

clues: Jacob met me at a well and agreed to work seven years to marry me.
On the wedding night my father substituted my older sister, so Jacob worked seven more years.
When we fled, I stole my father's household idols and hid them by sitting on them.
I died giving birth to my second son on the road near Bethlehem.

question: Which troubler of Israel am I?
reference: Joshua 7 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Achan')

clues: After the fall of Jericho, everything in it was to be devoted to destruction.
I took a beautiful robe, some silver, and a bar of gold, and buried them under my tent.
Israel was then routed at the small city of Ai, and the leaders tore their clothes.
I was found out by lot, and I and my household were stoned in a valley that still bears the name of my trouble.

question: Which woman of the Kenites am I?
reference: Judges 4-5 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Jael')

clues: I was the wife of Heber, and our clan was at peace with the enemy king.
A defeated commander fled on foot and I invited him into my tent and gave him milk.
When he fell into an exhausted sleep, I drove a tent peg through his temple.
Deborah's victory song called me the most blessed of women who dwell in tents.

question: Which woman from the Valley of Sorek am I?
reference: Judges 16 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Delilah')

clues: Each of the Philistine lords promised me 1,100 pieces of silver.
I pressed a powerful man day after day to tell me the source of his strength.
Three times he fed me a false answer before he finally told the truth.
While he slept on my knees, I had the seven braids of his hair shaved off.

question: Which prince of Israel am I?
reference: 2 Samuel 13 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Amnon No. 1')

clues: I was King David's firstborn son and the heir to the throne.
I pretended to be sick so that my half-sister Tamar would be sent to care for me.
I violated her and then despised her and threw her out.
Two years later my brother Absalom had his servants kill me at a sheepshearing feast.

question: Which would-be king am I?
reference: 1 Kings 1-2 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Adonijah No. 1')

clues: I was David's eldest surviving son, handsome, and never once disciplined by my father.
While my father lay dying, I held a feast and had myself proclaimed king.
Nathan and Bathsheba acted fast, and my younger brother was anointed instead.
Later I asked to marry Abishag, and the new king had me put to death for it.

question: Which grandson of Saul am I?
reference: 2 Samuel 4:4; 9; 19 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Mephibosheth No. 2')

clues: I was crippled in both feet at age five when my nurse dropped me while fleeing bad news.
King David searched for me so he could show kindness for my father's sake.
He gave back my grandfather's land and a permanent place at his own table.
My servant Ziba slandered me to the king during Absalom's revolt.

question: Which hesitant commander am I?
reference: Judges 4-5 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Barak')

clues: A prophetess called me to lead ten thousand men up Mount Tabor.
I told her I would only go if she came with me.
God threw the enemy chariots into confusion, and a flash flood in the Kishon swept them away.
She had warned me that the honor of the final blow would go to a woman.

question: Which scribe am I?
reference: Jeremiah 36; 43 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Baruch No. 1')

clues: I wrote down a prophet's words on a scroll as he dictated them.
When the king cut up and burned that scroll, I wrote it all again with more added.
I read the scroll aloud in the temple because the prophet was barred from going.
After Jerusalem fell, I was taken down to Egypt along with the prophet.

question: Which sanctuary town am I?
reference: Joshua 18:1; 1 Samuel 1-4; Jeremiah 7:12 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Shiloh No. 1')

clues: The tent of meeting stood in me for generations after the conquest of Canaan.
A grieving woman prayed here for a son, and here that son grew up serving the aging priest.
The ark was carried out from me into battle, captured by the Philistines, and never brought back.
Centuries later Jeremiah told Judah to go and look at what God had done to me.
